questions.q: Which pg_dump format flag produces a compressed archive designed for parallel and selective restore with pg_restore?
questions.explain: The custom format (-Fc) is a compressed, non-text archive built specifically for pg_restore, supporting parallel and selective restore.

questions.q: How do you restore a plain-format (-Fp) pg_dump backup?
questions.explain: Plain format is just a SQL script, so it's replayed with psql, not pg_restore (which is for custom, tar, and directory formats).

questions.q: What does pg_dump NOT capture, per this lesson, that pg_dumpall does?
options: Cluster-wide objects like roles and tablespaces
questions.explain: pg_dump only backs up a single database's objects and data; roles and tablespaces exist at the cluster level, which pg_dumpall covers.

options: Just the roles, role memberships, and tablespaces
A full dump of every database's data
A physical copy of the data directory
Only the current session's temporary tables
questions.explain: The --globals-only flag limits pg_dumpall's output to the cluster-wide setup, not per-database data.

questions.q: In a full disaster-recovery restore using logical backups, what is the correct order per this lesson?
options: Recreate the cluster, restore globals, then restore each database
Restore each database first, then recreate the cluster
Restore globals after all databases are already populated
Order doesn't matter since PostgreSQL resolves dependencies automatically
questions.explain: Databases often depend on roles already existing (as owners or grantees), so globals must be restored before individual databases.
